blocks.text: New Art Exchange in Nottingham, United Kingdom, invites artists, creatives, collectives and community groups to apply for its RESIDE 2027/28 programme, offering up to eight weeks of studio access, a £4,000 bursary and professional development support.
Open Call:
New Art Exchange (NAE) has announced the forthcoming open call for RESIDE 2027/28, its residency programme supporting artistic research, experimentation and the development of new creative ideas.

The programme gives artists and creative practitioners dedicated time, space, and resources to explore their practices, test new approaches, and build connections with NAE and the communities it serves.
Applications are welcomed from a broad range of disciplines, including visual arts, writing, curation, design, performance, activism and interdisciplinary practice.
NAE is particularly interested in proposals that engage with local communities and reflect its commitment to creativity, participation and social change.
Successful applicants will receive studio access, financial assistance, mentoring and opportunities to increase the visibility of their work through NAE’s professional networks and platforms.
Institutional Context:
New Art Exchange is a contemporary arts organisation based in Nottingham, United Kingdom, dedicated to championing diverse artistic voices and perspectives.
Through its exhibitions, public programmes and creative development initiatives, NAE supports artistic practices that encourage cultural exchange, community participation and social engagement.
RESIDE forms part of the organisation’s commitment to providing opportunities for artists and creative practitioners to develop their work within a supportive environment.
The programme encourages experimentation and collaboration while strengthening relationships between artists, cultural practitioners and local communities.
Eligibility and Criteria:
Applications are open to:
Artists and creative practitioners aged 18 and over.
Individual artists and collectives working across any artistic medium.
Writers, curators, designers, performers, activists and visual artists.
Practitioners working across multiple disciplines.
Collectives, provided at least one member meets the eligibility requirements.
NAE particularly encourages applications from artists and creative practitioners from the Global Ethnic Majority.
Proposals that establish meaningful connections with local communities and engage creativity, participation, and social change are especially welcome.
The programme is open to practitioners at different stages of their artistic development, with an emphasis on supporting research, experimentation and new approaches to creative practice.
Evaluation Process:
New Art Exchange welcomes proposals that demonstrate an interest in artistic experimentation, creative development and community engagement.
The organisation has expressed particular interest in projects that connect with local communities and align with its commitment to diverse perspectives and social change.

The opportunities webpage does not detail specific assessment criteria, jury composition, or selection procedures. Applicants should consult the official information pack and terms and conditions for further guidance.
Practical Information:
Application deadline: 9 December 2026
Residency period: June 2027 to April 2028
Duration: Up to eight weeks
Location: New Art Exchange, 39–41 Gregory Boulevard, Nottingham, NG7 6BE, United Kingdom
Successful applicants will receive:
Free access to NAE’s Studio Space for up to eight weeks.
A bursary of £4,000.
Mentoring and professional development support from the NAE team.
Opportunities to promote their work through NAE’s networks and platforms.
Dedicated time and space for research, experimentation and creative development.
Exact residency dates will be agreed upon with successful applicants.
Applications and Queries:
Applications for RESIDE 2027/28 close on 9 December 2026 .
Applicants are encouraged to review the official information pack and terms and conditions before submitting their proposals.
Applications will be accepted through the New Art Exchange website during the designated application period.
Programme information and applications: https://nae.org.uk/current-opportunities/
General enquiries: info@nae.org.uk
